conclusions: S01 and S02 are personal_local first-materialization fallbacks (provisioning/create lifecycle), not read-existing-asset resolver calls.

The personalFallback closure that contains S01/S02 runs ONLY when the security profile is personal_local AND the trusted locator (resolveAuthorizedToolCwd) returned no authorizedCwd; managed_enterprise fails closed to null with no legacy path fallback (resolveWorkspaceDirAfterAuthorization, src/gateway/workspace/handler-bridge.ts:872).

Both resolvers are pure host-path joins with no Catalog binding (resolveEmployeeBuiltinStewardWorkspaceDir at src/agents/builtin-steward/employee-isolation.ts:141; resolveAgentWorkspaceDir at src/agents/agent-scope.ts:270); the directory is created downstream by ensureAgentWorkspace -> fs.mkdir (src/agents/workspace.ts:337), so no Catalog binding pre-exists at the call site.

The call site holds only agentId / employeeOwnerId + cfg; it lacks the resourceId, catalog, tenantContext, tenantId, actor, and grant that resolveWorkspaceLocator/validateWorkspaceLocatorQuery require. Reading a locator binding before the workspace it names has been provisioned is circular.

The repository's own source of truth, LEGACY_LOCATOR_CALLER_MATRIX P1 (src/gateway/workspace-resolver/strict-locator.ts:555-568), pre-documents resolveAgentWorkspaceDir@get-reply.ts (shape agentId-only) as expectedReasonCode agent_id_slug_query_forbidden; a resolver swap at S02 is designed to fail closed, which confirms S02 is not honestly retirable by swap.
Adding catalog/grant/cfg parameters does not resolve the lifecycle ownership problem: the binding still has to be created by a provisioning owner before it can be read.
S01 and S02 must not be retired now; the accepted baseline stays 10 and must not be decremented (no 10 to 9, no 10 to 8).

S24/S25 accepted (landed) status and the batch-23 S26 semantic-gate conclusion must not be rolled back; Phase 1B, LIVE, production Catalog, schema v2, and production deploy stay locked; item 7 stays not-met.
